chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Bud Powell, Kenny Clarke and Benny Bailey sit in
summary: Bud Powell and Kenny Clarke worked at the Blue Note while Butler held court; Benny Bailey, in Paris with Quincy Jones's band, asked to sit in and ran through Stardust.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, about this time, Bud Powell came to the Paris scene?
Oh, Bud Powell was working at the Blue Note.
So he got there a little after you?
Benny Bailey was over there, too?
Oh, Benny Bailey, oh, that's my man. He come over there with his boys, this boy who writes all this pretty music. Boy from out West. Writes script music for Hollywood.
That's it, man. He comes with Quincy Jones' band. Now, this man --

Wait, one question. Did you happen to hear Clifford Brown when he was in Paris? He came to Paris '53, '52 or '53. He and Gigi Gryce, I think they came over there maybe -- maybe, I'm not sure, they may have come through there with Lionel Hampton's band?

Well, probably, but see, I couldn't have heard them because I was working too much here. But now Benny Bailey, now, I just come from the Casino de Paris, and they were sitting down there, Benny Bailey was sitting down there just as unconcerned. I always tried somebody to get me, see. They were mad because I was there so long. See, people get mad, 'What is he doing down there?' Kenny say, well, whatever he's doing down there, he's down there, so let him alone. Kenny's at the Blue Note, Don Byas is at the Blue Note, and Ray Robinson, he's at the other place, The Ringside, and all that stuff. But I

was over there, this was my thing. So I come in one night and changed the thing, come out fresh, put that old cologne on me. ("Hey,") Benny Bailey said, "Could I play one?" I said, "Yeah, man, come on." "Thank you, thank you."

Benny Bailey got up there and started playing "Star Dust" and we're running so much stuff, I said, look, stay right up there. "You stay right up there." See, I'm not going to get up there because that man was running too much stuff. He played the whole set. I said, ladies and gentlemen (inaudible) this is the man that's the greatest....beautiful.
